title: TDLR: Commission adopts rules (16 TAC 73.100, 2026 NEC)
publisher: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
keyFacts: Amended 16 TAC 73.100 adopts the 2026 NEC as the state electrical code, with a limited GFCI exception for certain outdoor outlets (notice body).
Adoption justification published 2026-08-28 Texas Register (51 TexReg 5776); effective 2026-09-01 (notice body).

title: Texas Register (2026-03-20) proposed amendment to 16 TAC 73.100 - 2026 NEC
publisher: Texas Secretary of State, Texas Register
keyFacts: Occupations Code 1305.101(a)(2) requires TDLR to adopt the most recent NEC as the state electrical code (preamble).
Proposed 73.100(a): effective 2026-09-01 TDLR adopts the 2026 NEC as approved by NFPA on 2025-09-09, replacing the 2023 NEC (rule text).
73.100(b): 2026 NEC 210.8(F) outdoor-outlet GFCI Exception No. 2 for listed HVAC equipment is adopted without its 2026-09-01 expiration (rule text).
History: TX exempted 2020 NEC 210.8(F) for HVAC nuisance tripping; 2023 NEC adopted as published (preamble).
notes: Proposed text; final adoption confirmed by tdlr-2026-nec-adoption-notice (a final adopted-text copy was not retrieved). Contains one short NEC exception quote inside a government publication.

title: TDLR Electricians Laws and Rules index
publisher: TDLR
keyFacts: Governing law: Texas Occupations Code Ch. 1305 (Electrical Safety and Licensing Act) and Ch. 51; rules 16 TAC Ch. 73 (page table).

title: TDLR Apply for a New Journeyman Electrician License
publisher: TDLR
keyFacts: With limited exemptions, anyone performing electrical work in Texas must be licensed (Who Must be Licensed).
Journeyman: 8,000 hours OJT under a Texas-licensed master electrician; may apply/test at 7,000 hours (Experience Qualifications).
Application by mail, $30 non-refundable; licenses valid one year, renewed annually (Application and Fee).

title: TDLR Apply for a New Master Electrician License
publisher: TDLR
keyFacts: Master: held journeyman license >= 2 years plus 12,000 hours OJT under a Texas master; Journeyman Industrial experience does not qualify (Experience Qualifications).
Holders of a municipal/regional master license may self-verify OJT for those years (Experience Qualifications).
Application by mail, $45 fee; annual renewal (Application and Fee).

title: TDLR Residential Wireman license
publisher: TDLR
keyFacts: Residential Wireman: 4,000 hours OJT under a Texas master electrician or residential wireman; $20 application fee (page body).

title: TDLR Apprentice Electrician license
publisher: TDLR
keyFacts: Electrical Apprentice license allows work under general supervision of a master, journeyman or residential wireman; online applicants with no convictions get a temporary license; annual renewal (page body).

title: TDLR Apply for a New Electrical Contractor License
publisher: TDLR
keyFacts: Contractor must employ a licensed Master Electrician of record (may be the owner); a master may serve only one contractor unless owning >50% of it (Master Electrician of Record).
Notify TDLR and designate a new master within 30 business days after the master of record leaves (Changing Your Master).
Liability insurance minimums: $300,000 per occurrence, $600,000 aggregate, $300,000 products/completed operations (Insurance Requirements).
Workers' comp proof, self-insurance certificate, or election of non-coverage filed with TDI (Worker's Compensation).

title: TDLR Transfer Your Out-of-State Electrician License to Texas (reciprocity)
publisher: TDLR
keyFacts: Master reciprocity: Alabama, Arkansas (master), Iowa (Class A master), Louisiana (state contractor), Mississippi (state contractor), Nebraska, North Carolina (master or unlimited contractor), Ohio, Tennessee (Electrical Contractor) (Other States Recognized).
Journeyman reciprocity: Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Nebraska, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Wyoming (Other States Recognized).
No reciprocity for any other license type; no reciprocity with California or Arizona listed (Other States Recognized).
Reciprocal master: passed that state's exam, held license >= 1 year, 12,000 h under a master, journeyman >= 2 years (1 year for AL, IA, MS, NE, OH, TN) (Requirements).
Reciprocal journeyman: passed that state's exam, held license >= 1 year, 8,000 h under a master (Requirements).
notes: This list (retrieved 2026-11-14) is broader than the national manifest's Feb-2026 note (adds AL, MS, OH, TN for master; Montana not listed for journeyman).

title: TDLR Electrician Exam Information
publisher: TDLR
keyFacts: Since 2025-03-11 the Journeyman exam has two parts: knowledge and calculations (notice).
Exams by PSI at Texas sites including Houston; applicants have one year from TDLR receipt of application to complete all requirements (Exam Eligibility; Locations).

title: TDLR Electrician Continuing Education
publisher: TDLR
keyFacts: 4 hours CE before each annual renewal for masters, journeymen, wiremen, maintenance, sign electricians and apprentices; contractors exempt (Do I Need CE).
CE must cover the NEC, Occupations Code Ch. 1305, 16 TAC Ch. 73, and NFPA 70E safety, from a TDLR-registered provider (Required Coursework).

title: TDLR Electricians FAQ
publisher: TDLR
keyFacts: A license is required even in unincorporated areas (1.1.3).
A state license is valid anywhere in Texas; a municipal license only within that city (9.1-9.2).

Cities may require a city license/fee only if you lack a TDLR license; Sec. 1305.201 limits fees cities charge state licensees but permits building-permit fees; cities may not require a local exam of state licensees (9.3).
In areas with municipal/regional licensing, report unlicensed work to that local authority first (8.1).

title: City of Houston Electrical Code - Administrative Code Provisions for the 2023 NEC (Ord. 2023-907)
publisher: City of Houston, Houston Public Works / Houston Permitting Center
keyFacts: Adopted by Ord. 2023-907, passed 2023-10-25, effective 2024-01-01 (cover p.).
Licensing per this code AND Occ. Code Ch. 1305 / 16 TAC 73, whichever is more restrictive (Sec. 101).

Permit exemptions include cord-and-plug equipment, like-for-like fixed motor/appliance replacement, temporary decorative lighting <=90 days, OCPD replacement same rating, and wiring <50 V and <=50 W (Sec. 301.2 items 1-13).
Annual maintenance permit available to building owners employing a full-time (>=36 h/week) electrical employee; expires Sept 30; keep work records 2 years (Sec. 301.4).
Only a licensed and city-registered electrical contractor may obtain a permit; application signed by the registered master electrician of record (Sec. 302.1).
Applications inactive after 180 days without permit; permits inactive 180 days after issue unless work started and inspected; expire after 2 years (Secs. 302.1.1, 303.4).
No concealment before inspection; final inspection required; city aims to inspect within 3 working days of request (Secs. 305.1-305.2).
No connection to energy source until approved; temporary connections limited to 90 days (Sec. 306).
City issues no new individual electrician licenses (only contractor); state licensees need no city registration EXCEPT state electrical/sign contractors must hold a city registration (Sec. 401.2).

Contractor registration requires a valid state contractor license, physical address, and full-time city-registered master; master of record may serve only one contracting business (Secs. 403.1, 403.7, 403.8, 404).
Carry license/registration documentation on your person while working (Sec. 401.4).

Local technical rules: meters 5-6 ft to center of dial on exterior; service disconnect handle 4 ft to 6 ft 7 in; electrodes per NEC 250.52(A)(1)-(A)(3) and (A)(7) must be supplemented by a rod electrode; no EMT buried in earth or in slab-on-grade concrete; saw pole >=60 A on 4x4 with 6 AWG service in conduit; no pool equipment/lighting >50 V in new pools; full-cutoff outdoor lighting near residential (Secs. 503-512).
NEC 240.91(B), 312.5(C) (exceptions adopted) and 645.25 not adopted (Sec. 513).
notes: Document text in Ch. 5 still cites the 'National Electrical Code, 2020 Edition' in Secs. 502-505/513 (apparent carry-over; strike-through markup may be lost in extraction). State law now makes the 2026 NEC the minimum (effective 2026-09-01); no Houston amendment document keyed to the 2026 NEC was found.

title: Houston Master Electrician Registration (HPWCODE1057)
publisher: City of Houston, Houston Public Works / Houston Permitting Center
keyFacts: Anyone wishing to perform electrical work in Houston must register with Electrical Inspections; registration valid 1 year, renewal required (Permit Description; Additional Information).
Requires copies of Texas master license and Texas contractor license plus notarized form CE-1189 (What You Need).
Since 2022-04-01 a master of record may hold a city contractor registration for only one business (Conditions).

title: Houston Electrical Contractor Registration (HPWCODE1051)
publisher: City of Houston, Houston Public Works / Houston Permitting Center
keyFacts: Master electricians, electrical contractors and appliance installers must register before working in Houston; 1-year validity (Permit Description).
Register by email (CE-1189), in person at 1002 Washington Ave, or by mail (Apply).
notes: Note tension with Sec. 401.2 (state-licensed individuals need no city registration) and TDLR FAQ 9.3; in practice registration is required for the contractor and master who pull permits.

title: Houston Circuit Panel Permit (HPWCODE1062)
publisher: City of Houston, Houston Public Works / Houston Permitting Center
keyFacts: Fee $91.06 or $9.39/panel (greater) + $33.56 admin; plan review and inspection required; valid 180 days (Fees; Additional Information).
Permits issued only to registered master electricians; apply via iPermits (What You Need; Apply Online).

title: Houston Generator Permit (HPWCODE1118)
publisher: City of Houston, Houston Public Works / Houston Permitting Center
keyFacts: Standby generator installs need an electrical permit by a registered contractor; kW-based fee + $33.56 admin; plan review and inspection required (page body).
Guideline CE-1060 Residential Standby Generator Permit & Inspection (Additional Resources).

title: Houston Temporary Cut-In Permit (HPWCODE1067)
publisher: City of Houston, Houston Public Works / Houston Permitting Center
keyFacts: Temporary cut-in gives temporary service before final; $94.00 + $33.56 admin; inspection required (page body).

title: Houston Annual Electrical Maintenance Permit (HPWCODE1048)
publisher: City of Houston, Houston Public Works / Houston Permitting Center
keyFacts: Renew in person at Electrical Inspections or by mail with form CE-1241 (page body).

title: Houston CE-1057 Electrical Building Permit Application

Contractor is responsible for scheduling inspections (p.1).
Example fees: meter loop & service up to 50 kW $94.00; outlets/fixtures $1.34 each; temporary saw pole $94.00 (p.1).
